req.title: Update only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to update a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that only the author of a post should be able to update it. This is a critical authorization check to ensure data integrity and user privacy. The test suite includes a positive case where the author updates their post, a negative case where a non-author attempts to update a post, and a boundary case to ensure the system behaves correctly at the edge of authorization rules.

tests.name: test_author_can_update_own_post
preconditions: Post with id 2 exists and is authored by Rahul
actions: Attempt to update post with id 2
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Log in as Rahul
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})

# Attempt to update Rahul's own post
r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated Body'})

assert r.status_code == 200

tests.name: test_non_author_cannot_update_post
preconditions: Post with id 2 exists and is authored by Rahul
actions: Attempt to update post with id 2
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Log in as Anjali
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})

# Attempt to update Rahul's post
r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Unauthorized Update', 'body': 'This should fail'})

assert r.status_code == 403
